venue_static.description: One revision of one venue's fixed properties, valid over [effective_from, effective_to). Revisions are append-only: a surface replacement or roof retrofit produces a NEW row with effective_from set to the install date and CLOSES the prior row's effective_to. A row is never edited in place. Many fields are deliberately nullable -- services/venue/venue/reference.py's docstring names each one and why it is null rather than guessed.

effective_to.description: Exclusive. null means this revision is current.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Not assumed to be US.

timezone.description: IANA zone, never a fixed offset: the season crosses the November DST transition and America/Phoenix does not observe it at all.

surface_product.description: The specific product and generation, e.g. field_turf_core. Null throughout the committed table: no source consulted distinguishes generations, and the spec names this the genuinely hard part.

home_team_ids.description: Tenants. Length 2 for a shared venue, 0 for a neutral-only site.

content_hash.description: sha256 over this revision's content fields, excluding venue_id and the validity window. A new snapshot is appended only when this changes, which is what keeps a daily static-reference re-read from filling the lake with identical objects.

venue_game_assignment.description: Which building one game is actually played in. Exists because "the home team's stadium" is wrong roughly a dozen times a year -- London, Munich, Sao Paulo, neutral-site relocations, and both MetLife tenants. Carries the resolved revision's window so the spec's read-time join (no game may resolve to a revision whose window excludes its kickoff) is a field comparison on one row rather than a scan of the venue_static history.

is_international.description: The venue's country differs from the league's home country.
